decision_rule: PRIMARY (replication): compute scaffold fidelity exactly as in A12 (Spearman rank corr of pairwise centroid distances at compress-end vs best-known optimum across methods). One-sided test: Spearman(fidelity, harden_gap_to_optimum) < -0.3 with p < 0.05 on these 10 held-out instances -> the A12 rule replicates as a predictive relationship. SECONDARY (exploratory, not confirmatory): proxy fidelity using best-of-16 rigid arrangement as D_opt stand-in; assess whether it predicts win/tie a priori. If primary fails, the A12 rule does not generalize and is reported as overfit to the discovery set.
hypothesis: The A12 scaffold-fidelity rule generalizes: on 10 held-out instances (no data in the 49-instance discovery set), higher scaffold fidelity predicts smaller harden gap to the optimum. These instances span ltri/star5/cross in squares, convex rare-event territory (squ/tri n=12,13), and triangle containers - chosen to include expected wins, ties, and losses.
question: Does the scaffold-fidelity rule predict on held-out instances?
title: Held-out validation of the scaffold-fidelity rule
